content.thinking: I need to understand the issue.
Need to update the issue-service, event-registry, instrumentation, rate limits, and search page query path. Also need to configure the advanced_search feature flag.

A discrepancy exists between client and server search behavior. The client treats colons as free text when advanced mode is off, but the search service throws an error if the query contains a colon in that state.

The error message is "Field-scoped search is not included in this plan". Rate limits, org scope checks, permission assertions, Zod validation, API route flags, and ForbiddenActionError are also involved.

Status changes do not reindex because they emit issue.status_changed rather than issue.updated. Title edits do reindex since they emit issue.updated. The stored searchable content is title plus description, so status is not indexed.

Search listeners rebuild the index from the persisted database row rather than using the event payload. The issue.updated event only carries changedFields, not the new title.

Upsert updates content, projectId, and indexedAt within the existing (org, kind, subjectId) record.

SQLite LIKE is case-insensitive for ASCII text, though the code snippet explicitly lowercases queries.

The startup sequence registers instrumentation first, then event handlers, then search listeners.

The scheduler enqueues search-reindex payloads as empty objects. The queue handler may not receive the orgId.

The "moments later" path is synchronous. It emits during the write and awaits before updateIssue returns. The index row is upserted unless a handler throws. Swallowed errors let the index lag behind the write. The reindex job repairs this.

The search reindex listener only handles issue subjectKind. Search queries are refused for empty or overly long terms, org scope mismatches, missing read permissions, and rate limit exhaustion.

A colon in the query string is refused when advanced search is disabled. The server rejects field-scoped queries before they reach the index. The client parser handles colons differently, but the API passes the raw string through unchanged.

content.text:
A title edit becomes searchable in the same request that saves it. The `search_index` table is a denormalised copy, and `search()` refuses some syntactically ordinary strings before it ever runs that copy.

## How the copy stays in step

Process start calls `register()` in `src/instrumentation.ts` (Node runtime only). That calls `registerEventHandlers()` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`, which calls `registerSearchListeners()` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts` once. Those listeners sit on the in-process bus in `src/lib/event-bus.ts`.

A title change goes through `updateIssue` in `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` (the server action is `src/actions/issues/update-issue.ts`):

1. `assertOrgScope`, then `issueRepo.findIssueById`, then `assertCan(..., "issue:update", ...)` and `assertNotArchived`.
2. `issueRepo.updateIssue` writes the issues row.
3. `emit("issue.updated", ...)` publishes an envelope with `orgId`, `issueId`, `projectId`, and `changedFields`. The new title is not on the event.
4. `emit` awaits every subscriber with `Promise.allSettled`. A thrown indexer does not roll back the issue write; the error goes to the bus error sinks.

The `issue.updated` handler in `registerSearchListeners` ignores the payload body and calls `issueRepo.findIssueById` again. If that row exists, `indexIssue` runs. The same re-read-then-index pattern is used for `issue.created`. `issue.archived` calls `removeFromIndex` instead. `issue.status_changed` and `issue.assigned` are not subscribed, so a status or assignee change does not touch the index. Un-assigning does, because `assignIssue` emits `issue.updated` when `assigneeId` is null.

`indexIssue` calls `upsertSearchDocument` in `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts`. That looks up the row by `(orgId, subjectKind = "issue", subjectId)`, not by index id. A hit updates `content`, `projectId`, and `indexedAt`. A miss inserts a new ULID id plus those fields. The same upsert is used for comments (`comment.body` only, `projectId` null) and projects (`name` plus description, `projectId` set to the project id), driven by `comment.created` / `comment.deleted` and `project.created` / `project.archived`.

A slower repair path exists beside this. `search.reindex_requested` is handled only when `subjectKind === "issue"`, and again re-reads the issue. `runSearchReindexJob` in `src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts` walks one org’s projects, issues, and comments (page size 100, first page only) and calls `indexProject`, `indexIssue`, and `indexComment`. The scheduler in `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts` enqueues `"search-reindex"` at most once every 1440 minutes. The title a colleague finds moments later comes from the awaited `issue.updated` handler, not from that job.

## What the copy stores

The table is `searchIndex` (`search_index`) in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`, created in `src/server/db/migrate.ts`. Each row is:

- `id` — ULID primary key
- `orgId` — from `tenantColumns` in `src/server/db/schema/_shared.ts`
- `subjectKind` — `"issue" | "comment" | "project"`
- `subjectId` — the issue, comment, or project id
- `projectId` — nullable
- `content` — for an issue, `title` and `description ?? ""` joined with a newline
- `indexedAt` — ISO-8601 text

There is an index on `(org_id, subject_kind)`. Status, assignee, labels, and priority are not stored. The first line of `content` is later treated as the hit title.

## What a query goes through

Three entry points call the same `search()` in `search-service.ts`: the search page `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/search/page.tsx`, the server action `searchAction` in `src/actions/search/search.ts`, and `GET` in `src/app/api/search/route.ts`.

On the page, `loadTenantContext` loads the org and actor, `isEnabled("advanced_search", ...)` decides kinds, and `searchQuerySchema` in `src/schemas/search.ts` requires `q` of 1–200 characters. Kinds are `["issue", "comment", "project"]` when the flag is on and `["issue"]` otherwise, with `limit` 30. An invalid parse never reaches `search()`; the page renders “That query is not valid”.

`search()` then, in order:

1. `assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)`.
2. `assertCan(actor, "issue:read", orgResource(input.orgId))`.
3. `consumeRateLimit(input.orgId, "search:query")`. That bucket, in `src/lib/rate-limit.ts`, holds 120 tokens and refills 60 per minute. If `allowed` is false it throws `Search rate limit reached; try again after ${resetAt}`.
4. `orgRepo.findOrgById`, then `isEnabled("advanced_search", ...)`. The flag is defined in `src/config/feature-flags.ts` as a plan strategy with `minPlan: "enterprise"`, overridable via `org.settings.enabledFlagOverrides`. `isEnabled` in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` returns true for an override or when `planAtLeast` says the org plan is at least enterprise.
5. If `input.q` contains `:` and the flag is off, it throws `Field-scoped search is not included in this plan` and never queries the table. That is the refusal of a perfectly ordinary-looking string. `status:done` is the intended field syntax, but the check is any colon, so a title search such as `fix: login` is refused on free and growth plans. The client parser `parseSearchQuery` in `src/components/domain/search/query-syntax.ts` does the opposite when `advanced` is false: it keeps the colon as literal text. The server does not use that parser. `searchAction` only narrows `kinds` to `"issue"` when the flag is off; it still forwards `q` unchanged into `search()`, so the colon check still fires. The palette route does the same, and also returns `forbidden` when `can(..., "org:read", ...)` fails or `command_palette` is off, and `validation_failed` when `orgSlug` or `q` is missing or the schema rejects the string.
6. `searchRepo.searchDocuments` filters with `orgPredicate` on `orgId`, `LIKE %q%` on `content`, optional `subjectKind` and `projectId`, then keyset-pages by `indexedAt` descending and `id` descending.
7. Each row becomes a `SearchHit`: `kind`, `subjectId`, title = first line of `content`, `snippetAround` (60 characters on each side of a case-insensitive match), and `hrefFor` (`/issues/${id}`, `/comments/${id}`, or `/projects/${id}`).

6. `searchRepo.searchDocuments` filters with `orgPredicate` on `orgId`, `LIKE %q%` on `content`, optional `subjectKind` and `projectId`, then keyset-pages by `indexedAt` descending and `id` descending.
7. Each row becomes a `SearchHit`: `kind`, `subjectId`, title = first line of `content`, `snippetAround` (60 characters on each side of a case-insensitive match), and `hrefFor` (`/issues/${id}`, `/comments/${id}`, or `/projects/${id}`).
